ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are four circles with the same radius, located respectively at the upper-left, upper-right, lower-left, and lower-right positions; adjacent circles are tangent near the midpoints of the sides of the square. The four vertices of the square correspond to the centers of the four circles, and the gray shaded region is inside the square and outside the four circles. Reasoning: Each circle has radius 3, so the distance between two adjacent circle centers is one diameter, namely 6, so the side length of the square is 6. The area of the square is 6^2=36. Each of the four corners of the square is occupied by a 90-degree sector of radius 3, and the four 90-degree sectors together equal one whole circle, with area π·3^2=9π. Therefore the shaded area is 36-9π≈36-28.274=7.726, closest to 7.7.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a square whose four vertices are the centers of the four radius-3 circles. From the picture, adjacent circles are tangent at the midpoints of the square sides, so the square side length is one diameter, 6. The shaded region is the part of this square left after removing the four quarter-circles cut out by the circles at the four corners. Compute square area minus four 90-degree sectors: 6^2 - 4(π·3^2/4) = 36 - 9π ≈ 7.7.
